title: Token Trace Playbook: Story-driven Cost Explorer & Pricing Presets
creator: Ava Moritz
description: Design a story-driven Token Cost Explorer focused on narrative exports and opinionated pricing presets. Deliverables: (1) high-fidelity console screens for token-level breakdown (per-message, prefix vs generation, model variant), (2) an export/CSV schema and an export wizard with role-aware defaults, (3) a pricing-presets panel (SKU templates, marginal ratebands) that product teams can apply to slices, and (4) prototype flows for canary rollouts and bulk attribution adjustments. Goals: make per-token economics understandable to engineers and finance stakeholders, reduce support tickets caused by opaque chargebacks, and provide export formats that feed downstream chargeback systems. Non-goals: full billing system implementation (this ticket is UI/prototype only).
comments: 2026-02-10 — Kickoff: aligned with PM (Lena Ortiz) and Eng (Marco Silva) on scope. Agreed to prioritize CSV export schema and a compact ledger UI that supports sampling for very large result sets.

2026-02-17 — Research summary: reviewed customer support logs (Q4) and found 28% of billing disputes reference 'missing context' in token attribution. Benchmarked competitor consoles (Acme AI, Nebula Endpoints) and noted they either (a) flatten at the request level or (b) expose raw token logs — both options confused users. Decision: adopt hybrid approach: story rows (human-friendly) + expandable raw trace.

2026-02-24 — Design draft v1 uploaded to Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/4QbHnX/Token-Trace-Playbook-v1 — includes: narrative top bar (scenario name, applied pricing preset), cost waterfall sparkline per conversation, and an 'attribution ribbon' showing model, prompt slice, and caching effect. Initial feedback from PM: prefer clearer SKU mapping and a compact export mode for finance teams.

2026-03-02 — Engineering sync: ENG-21021 (backend token attribution API) will expose these fields: request_id, user_id, model_variant, input_tokens, output_tokens, prefix_hits, kv_cache_hit_percent, quant_profile. Eng requested UI schema to avoid extra iterations. Added 'export field mapping' table to Confluence.

2026-03-04 — Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Token+Trace+Playbook — contains CSV schema, pricing-presets JSON example, and role-based export rules. Noted trade-off: exporting unaggregated per-token rows could exceed S3 ingestion quotas — we will provide 3 export modes: summary, expanded (grouped by request), raw (sampled by rate).

2026-03-07 — Design review with Finance beta users: they asked for effective per-1000-token normalization and a way to map cost buckets to GL codes. Action: add 'pricing preset' editor that allows adding GL code and default rateband anchor.
2026-03-09 — Accessibility pass: updated color contrast for sparkline overlays; made export dropdown keyboard accessible. Added aria labels for trace rows and pricing presets list.

2026-03-11 — In Review: UX critique from Design Lead (Maya Chen): request to reduce cognitive load by collapsing less-used columns behind a 'detail' chevron and show a single-line summary per trace by default. Also suggested adding a small inline calculator to preview cost impact when switching presets.

2026-03-12 — Follow-up tasks: (a) create a lightweight interactive prototype for the inline calculator (Ravi), (b) finalize CSV column ordering and add sample dataset (Ava), (c) coordinate with ENG to add a 'preview_export' endpoint (ENG-21021) that streams first 200 rows for the UI preview. Linked PR placeholder: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4567

Notes: We should consider retention limits when designing the sample/expanded exports (legal/regulatory). For Private deployments, include a toggle that marks exports as 'local-only' to avoid cross-region data egress.
